basics.description: OpenSteward is a self-hosted unified integration platform. This offer deploys the OpenSteward Helm chart onto an existing AKS cluster via a Kubernetes-app (cluster extension). Images are pulled from the Marketplace ACR, digest-pinned. **Bring Your Own License (BYOL): this package collects no marketplace metering or entitlement.** The OpenSteward license is a file verified offline, named as a Kubernetes Secret in the License step.

options.text: Select the AKS cluster to install OpenSteward into. The cluster must already have an ingress controller, cert-manager (for TLS), and — if you choose External Secrets — the External Secrets Operator and Workload Identity (OIDC issuer + a federated managed identity). See the offer README.

subLabel.preValidation: Configure the target cluster and image source

options.text: Images are served from the Marketplace-managed ACR and pinned by multi-arch digest. The chart's image.registry is overridden to that ACR; image.digest pins the exact signed build. You normally leave these at their defaults.

elements.name: imageRegistry
elements.label: Image registry (registry + owner)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value image.registry. The single overridable '<registry>/<owner>' prefix; the chart's image helper appends the service name, forming '<registry>/<owner>/<service>' (i.e. printf '%s/%s' image.registry <service>). Defaults to the Marketplace-mirrored registry.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a lowercase registry host and path, e.g. mcr.microsoft.com/open-steward.

elements.name: imageDigest
elements.label: Image digest (sha256:...)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value image.digest. When set, every service is pulled by digest ('<registry>/<owner>/<service>@<digest>', where the helper appends '/<service>' to image.registry) for reproducible, cosign-verifiable deploys. Leave blank to fall back to the image tag.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be empty or a digest like sha256: followed by 64 hex characters.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Image tag (used only if no digest)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value image.tag. Ignored when a digest is provided. Empty falls back to the chart appVersion. Pin a release like 0.1.0.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid image tag, or leave blank to use the chart appVersion.

elements.name: databaseMode
elements.label: Database mode
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value database.mode. 'postgres' makes the stateful services stateless and points them at a managed Azure Database for PostgreSQL. 'sqlite' gives each stateful service a PVC and a single replica — trials only.

elements.name: dbExistingSecret
elements.label: Existing DATABASE_URL secret name
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value database.external.existingSecret. Name of a Kubernetes Secret in the release namespace holding the Postgres connection string. Create it from your Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server output before installing.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Kubernetes Secret name (lowercase alphanumerics and '-').

elements.name: dbSecretKey
elements.label: Key within that secret
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value database.external.secretKey. The data key inside the secret that holds the connection string.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Kubernetes Secret data key.

elements.name: dbStorageClass
elements.label: PVC storage class (SQLite mode)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value database.persistence.storageClass. Storage class for the per-service PVCs in SQLite mode. 'managed-csi' is the default Azure disk CSI class.

elements.name: redisEnabled
elements.label: Enable Redis (required to scale integration-server past 1 replica)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value redis.enabled. integration-server shares a per-API-key rate-limit budget across replicas via Redis. Required before scaling it beyond one replica.

elements.name: redisUrl
elements.label: Redis URL
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value redis.url. Azure Cache for Redis SSL endpoint, e.g. rediss://<name>.redis.cache.windows.net:6380.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a redis:// or rediss:// URL.

subLabel.preValidation: Choose how app secrets are supplied

options.text: OpenSteward runs with NODE_ENV=production and fails closed: a weak or missing JWT_SECRET / SESSION_SECRET / STORE_SECRET crash-loops the pod rather than running insecurely. Each key must be >=32 chars with real entropy. STORE_SECRET is the data-at-rest key — set it once and never rotate it casually.

elements.name: secretsSource
elements.label: Secrets source
elements.defaultValue: Azure Key Vault via External Secrets (recommended)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.source. Controls how the app secrets land in the single <release>-secrets Kubernetes Secret the pods read.

allowedValues.label: Azure Key Vault via External Secrets (recommended)

elements.name: esProvider
elements.label: External Secrets provider
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.externalSecrets.provider. For the Azure Marketplace listing this is fixed to Azure Key Vault.

elements.name: esVaultUrl
elements.label: Key Vault URI
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.externalSecrets.azure.vaultUrl. The full vault URI, e.g. https://<vault>.vault.azure.net. From the Bicep output keyVaultUri.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a Key Vault URI like https://myvault.vault.azure.net.

elements.name: esTenantId
elements.label: Azure AD tenant ID
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.externalSecrets.azure.tenantId. The AAD tenant GUID that owns the Key Vault.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a tenant GUID.

elements.name: esRemoteSecretName
elements.label: Key Vault secret name (JSON blob)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.externalSecrets.remoteSecretName. A single Key Vault secret whose value is a JSON object with keys JWT_SECRET / SESSION_SECRET / STORE_SECRET (and optionally ADMIN_SECRET). ESO syncs it into the pod Secret.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Key Vault secret name (alphanumerics and '-').

elements.name: esCreateStore
elements.label: Let the chart render the (Cluster)SecretStore
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.externalSecrets.createStore. When checked, the chart renders the ESO SecretStore that authenticates to Key Vault using the chart ServiceAccount's Workload Identity. Uncheck to reuse an operator-managed store (then name it below).

elements.name: esSecretStoreName
elements.label: Existing (Cluster)SecretStore name
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.externalSecrets.secretStore.name. Required only when you DON'T let the chart render the store — the name of your operator-managed ClusterSecretStore that ESO reads Key Vault through. Ignored when the chart renders its own store.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid (Cluster)SecretStore name.

elements.name: existingSecretName
elements.label: Existing Kubernetes Secret name
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value secrets.existingSecret. Name of an operator-managed Secret (e.g. from Sealed Secrets / SOPS) holding JWT_SECRET / SESSION_SECRET / STORE_SECRET.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Kubernetes Secret name.

options.text: Generate mode runs a pre-install hook Job that creates and maintains <release>-secrets. It never overwrites an existing STORE_SECRET. The resulting Secret is not Helm-owned, so uninstall leaves it. Use for trials; prefer Key Vault for production.

subLabel.preValidation: Configure hosts, TLS, and public URLs

options.text: admin-api is never exposed (ClusterIP only). The Admin UI host routes to the 'admin' service; the API host routes to 'integration-server'. Public URLs must match these hosts so SSO callbacks and cross-app links resolve from the browser.

elements.name: ingressClassName
elements.label: Ingress class name
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value ingress.className. On AKS with the app-routing add-on use 'webapprouting.kubernetes.io'; with a self-managed ingress-nginx use 'nginx'.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid ingress class name.

elements.name: adminHost
elements.label: Admin UI host (routes to admin)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value ingress.hosts[0].host with service 'admin', and to publicUrls.adminUi. The public DNS name for the admin console.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a fully qualified domain name, e.g. admin.example.com.

elements.name: apiHost
elements.label: API host (routes to integration-server)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value ingress.hosts[1].host with service 'integration-server', and to publicUrls.integrationServer. The canonical Connect-Link / public API domain.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a fully qualified domain name, e.g. api.example.com.

elements.name: adminApiPublicUrl
elements.label: SSO public base URL (admin-api callbacks)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value publicUrls.adminApi (SSO_PUBLIC_BASE_URL). Where IdPs send SAML ACS / OIDC callbacks. admin-api is not ingress-exposed by the chart; front it with your own host/route if SSO is used.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an https:// URL or leave blank.

elements.name: tlsMode
elements.label: TLS
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value ingress.tls. cert-manager provisions per-host certs from a ClusterIssuer; or reference an existing TLS Secret; or disable in-cluster TLS (e.g. when an external LB terminates).

elements.name: tlsClusterIssuer
elements.label: cert-manager ClusterIssuer
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value ingress.tls.certManager.clusterIssuer. Name of the cert-manager ClusterIssuer (a cluster prerequisite), e.g. letsencrypt-prod.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid ClusterIssuer name.

elements.name: tlsExistingSecret
elements.label: Existing TLS secret name
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value ingress.tls.existingSecret. Name of a Kubernetes TLS Secret covering the hosts above.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Kubernetes Secret name.

subLabel.preValidation: Bind the chart ServiceAccount to a managed identity

options.text: When secrets come from Key Vault via External Secrets, the chart ServiceAccount must federate to a user-assigned managed identity that has 'Key Vault Secrets User' on the vault. Paste its client ID below. Not required for existing-secret or generate modes.

elements.name: workloadIdentityClientId
elements.label: Managed identity client ID
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value serviceAccount.annotations.[azure.workload.identity/client-id]. The clientId (GUID) of the user-assigned managed identity ESO federates to. From the Bicep output managedIdentityClientId.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter the managed identity client ID (GUID).

subLabel.preValidation: Optional: name the Secret holding your OpenSteward license

options.text: OpenSteward verifies a license file offline; nothing is metered or reported. Without one it runs in community mode: all current verticals, 1 connection, 1 tenant. Create a Secret in the release namespace from your license file (kubectl create secret generic opensteward-license --from-file=license.key=./license.key) and name it below. The mount is optional, so you can name the Secret now and create it later, then restart integration-server once.

elements.name: licenseSecretName
elements.label: License secret name (optional)
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value license.existingSecret. Name of a Kubernetes Secret holding the license file, mounted read-only on integration-server only. Empty = community mode.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Kubernetes Secret name (lowercase alphanumerics and '-'), or leave it empty.

elements.name: licenseSecretKey
elements.label: Key within that secret
elements.toolTip: Maps to Helm value license.secretKey. The data key inside the secret that holds the license file.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid Kubernetes Secret data key.
